Conventions
Handles. A creregex (a compiled pattern), a crecaptures (what a match captured) and a crematches (a global
  search) are opaque, created by the library and freed by the caller with their free function (creregexfree,
  crecapturesfree, crematchesfree). Each free function takes NULL and does nothing. A creregex is immutable:
  any number of threads may use one at once. A crecaptures or a crematches is used by one thread at a time.
Text in. UTF-8 text is a pointer and a length in bytes, checked to be UTF-8 (CREINVALIDUTF8 otherwise). The
  functions with the suffix utf16 take UTF-16 text instead, a pointer and a length in code units, which may hold
  lone surrogates and is not checked. A pointer may be NULL when its length is 0. Nothing is transcoded: positions
  are in the units of the text, bytes of UTF-8 or UTF-16 code units.
Text out. A borrowed string is a crestr (or crestr16), not NUL-terminated, valid for as long as its function
  says. An owned string is a crestring (or crestring16), NUL-terminated, which the caller frees with
  crestringfree (or crestring16free); the pieces of a split are a crepieces (or crepieces16), freed with
  crepiecesfree (or crepieces16free).
Status. Every function that can fail returns a crestatus, CREOK or why it failed, with a message in
  thread-local storage (crelasterrormessage, crelasterroroffset). On failure each out-parameter is set to
  its empty value (NULL, false, CREUNSET or {NULL, 0}). No Rust panic crosses into the caller: a bug in the
  library is CREPANIC, and the library remains usable.
Matching. A pattern is read as new RegExp(pattern, flags) reads it, and a match is the one exec finds. Without
  the u or v flag a pattern is matched by UTF-16 code unit, so over UTF-8 a match can start or end between the
  halves of a character beyond the Basic Multilingual Plane; such a position is the offset of the character's
  third byte. The g flag makes creregexreplace replace every match; the y flag makes a match start where the
  search starts.
Limits. A pattern over a limit of size is refused (CREPATTERNTOOLARGE). A regular expression has a match
  timeout, as a Regex of .NET has: the time each match may take, given by creregexnewwithtimeout or for every
  regular expression by cresetdefaultmatchtimeout, and none unless one of them gives one. A match that reaches
  it, or whose backtracking memory reaches CREMAXSTACK entries, is CREMATCHLIMIT, which is not an answer, from
  whichever function matched. The functions with the suffix limit take a limit of their own in milliseconds (0
  for the regular expression's timeout). Without a timeout a match has no limit of time or of memory, so a program
  that matches patterns or texts from outside should set one. A pattern without a backreference takes time in
  proportion to its size times the text.
Constants and types
CREVERSIONMAJOR, CREVERSIONMINOR, CREVERSIONPATCH
The header's version: compare with creversion(), the library's.
CREMAXPATTERNLENGTH, CREMAXNESTING, CREMAXSIZE
The limits of size of a pattern: its length in bytes, the depth its groups nest to, and the size counted for it as
it is read. A pattern over any of them is CREPATTERNTOOLARGE.
CREMAXSTACK
The entries the backtracking stack of a match with a limit may reach before the match is CREMATCHLIMIT.
CREUNSET
The start and the end of a group that did not take part in a match, and of no match.
CRESPLITALL
The limit of creregexsplit that keeps every piece, as split(separator) with no limit.
CREEDITIONCURRENT, CREEDITIONES2020
The edition of ECMA-262 whose grammar a pattern is read with (creregexnewwithoptions): today's, the default, or
ECMAScript 2020's, which JSON Schema 2020-12 names. The 2020 grammar refuses what later editions added, and nothing
else: the d and v flags, modifier groups, a group name used twice, and a property name or value that is not in the
edition's tables.
CREUNICODEDEFAULT, CREUNICODE13, CREUNICODE17, CREUNICODE18, CREUNICODELATEST
The version of Unicode whose tables a pattern is read with (creregexnewwithoptions), independent of the
edition: the default (the version of the V8 the answers are held to, 17 today), 13, 17, 18, or the latest the
library carries (18 today).
crestatus
The outcome of a call: CREOK, or why it failed (the details are in crelasterrormessage).
CREOK
The call succeeded.
CREINVALIDARGUMENT
A NULL handle or pointer, a value out of range (a start beyond the text or inside a character), a misaligned
UTF-16 pointer, or a handle used with the wrong regular expression.
CREINVALIDUTF8
Text that is not UTF-8 (crelasterroroffset is the offset of the first invalid byte).

Title: "C++: API reference"
The C++ API: the header , namespace , generated from its declarations
and their comments by . Getting started shows it at work.
Conventions
A regex is a compiled pattern, read as new RegExp(pattern, flags) reads it. It is immutable, so any number of
  threads may use one at once, and copying one shares the compiled pattern rather than compiling it again.
Text is any std::basicstringview of char or char8t (UTF-8, checked: text that is not UTF-8 throws) or of
  char16t (UTF-16, not checked, lone surrogates and all), and so a std::basicstring or a pointer to a
  NUL-terminated string of those. On Windows, wchart text is UTF-16. Nothing is transcoded: positions are in the
  units of the text, bytes of UTF-8 or UTF-16 code units.
A match is the one exec finds. Without the u or v flag a pattern is matched by UTF-16 code unit, so over UTF-8 a
  match can start or end between the halves of a character beyond the Basic Multilingual Plane; such a position is
  the offset of the character's third byte.
Failures throw corvus::ecma262::regexerror, whose code() says why (std::errorcode, in ecma262::category()). A
  pattern that is not valid is errc::invalidpattern; a match that reaches its limit of time or of backtracking
  memory is errc::matchlimit.
A regex has a match timeout, as a Regex of .NET has: the constructor that takes a std::chrono::milliseconds, or
  regex::setdefaultmatchtimeout for every regex made after it (none unless set). Every member that matches gives
  each of its matches the timeout, and the overloads that take a std::chrono::milliseconds give one match a limit
  of their own. Without a timeout a match has no limit of time or of memory, so give a pattern or a text from
  outside one.
A pattern is read in the grammar of an edition (edition::current, today's, or edition::es2020, which JSON Schema
  2020-12 names) and under a version of Unicode (unicodeversion::v8, the version of the V8 the answers are held to,
  17 today; v13, v17, v18; or latest, 18 today), each independent of the other and settled when it is compiled, so
  that they cost a match nothing: regex::options carries them with a match timeout. regex::trycompile is the form
  that does not throw, and takes the options too, so a validator needs no default timeout.
A global search (findall, capturesall) is a range that keeps the regex alive but not the text, as a
  std::stringview does not: the text must outlive it.
errc
Why a call failed: the C library's statuses other than CREOK.
category
The error category of errc.
makeerrorcode
regexerror
What a call that failed throws: the reason (code(), an errc), the C library's message (what()) and, for text that
is not UTF-8, the offset of the first invalid byte (offset()).
regexerror::regexerror
regexerror::reason
The reason, as an errc.
regexerror::offset
The offset of the first byte that is not UTF-8, for errc::invalidutf8; otherwise 0.
edition
The edition of ECMA-262 whose grammar a pattern is read with: today's, the default, or ECMAScript 2020's. The 2020
grammar refuses what later editions added: the d and v flags (errc::invalidflags), modifier groups, a name given to
more than one group, and property names that are not in its edition's tables (each errc::invalidpattern).
unicodeversion
The version of Unicode whose tables a pattern is read with (its properties and its case folding), independent of
the edition: v8, the version of the V8 the answers are held to (17 today); 13, 17 or 18; or latest, the latest the C
library carries (18 today).
unicodeversions
The versions of Unicode a pattern can be read with; the one unicodeversion::v8 stands for; and the one
unicodeversion::latest stands for.
npos
The position of no match and of a group that did not take part.
match
Where a match or a group is in its text: start to end, in the text's units (bytes of UTF-8, or UTF-16 code
units). A group that did not take part is npos to npos, and is false.
match::start
match::operator bool
Whether the group took part in the match.
match::length
The length in units (0 for a group that did not take part).
match::in
The part of the text, which must be the text the match was found in.
match::operator==
nolimit
The limit of split that keeps every piece, as split(separator) with no limit.
basiccaptures
What a match captured: each group by number (0 is the whole match) and by name, with the text it was found in.
It is what regex::captures returns, and what a capturesall range gives for each match (reused from one match to
the next, so copy what must outlive the step).
basiccaptures::size
The number of groups, the whole match among them.
basiccaptures::operator[]
Where group i is (false when it did not take part, or there is no such group).
Where the group of the name is (of the groups that share it, the one that took part).

The module , generated from its public declarations and their comments by

Conventions
ECMA-262 (JavaScript) regular expressions for Fortran: a binding to the corvus-regex-ecma262 C library, through
ISOCBINDING, with the grammar and the answers of RegExp.
A pattern is compiled once into a regext, which matches any number of texts, from any number of threads. Text is
UTF-8 in a character variable, positions in bytes, or UTF-16 in an integer(int16) array, positions in code units
(which may hold lone surrogates). Positions are from 1, and a matcht's start and end are inclusive, so that
text(m%start:m%end) is the match; an empty match ends one before it starts.
Every handle frees what it holds when it is finalized. Assigning one regext to another compiles the same pattern
again; a capturest may not be copied.
A procedure that can fail takes the optional arguments stat and errmsg, as the intrinsic statements do: stat is
CREOK or the status of the failure, and errmsg its message. When stat is absent, a failure stops the program
with the message (error stop).
Constants
bindingversion
The version of this binding.
CREEDITIONCURRENT, CREEDITIONES2020
The edition of ECMA-262 whose grammar a pattern is read with (the C library's CREEDITION): today's, the default,
or ECMAScript 2020's, which JSON Schema 2020-12 names. The 2020 grammar refuses what later editions added: the d
and v flags, modifier groups, a name given to more than one group, and property names not in its tables.
CREUNICODEDEFAULT, CREUNICODE13, CREUNICODE17, CREUNICODE18, CREUNICODELATEST
The version of Unicode whose tables a pattern is read with, independent of the edition (the C library's
CREUNICODE): the default, which is the version of the V8 the answers are held to, 13, 17, 18, or the latest the
library carries.
unicodeversions, defaultunicodeversion, latestunicodeversion
The versions of Unicode a pattern can be read with; the one CREUNICODEDEFAULT stands for; and the one
CREUNICODELATEST stands for.
CREOK, CREINVALIDARGUMENT, CREINVALIDUTF8, CREINVALIDPATTERN, CREINVALIDFLAGS, CREPATTERNTOOLARGE, CREMATCHLIMIT, CREPANIC
The outcome of a call (crestatus).
Types
matcht
Where a match or a group is, from 1, start and end inclusive: text(m%start:m%end). A group that did not take
part has matched = .false. (and start 0, end -1).
piecet
A piece of a split of UTF-8 text: defined = .false. for a group that did not take part (undefined in the array
split returns).
piece16t
A piece of a split of UTF-16 text.
utf8textt
A UTF-8 text, checked once when utf8text makes it, which regext's methods search without checking it again: a
character argument is checked on every call, a read of the whole text each time. Only utf8text gives one a text,
so it always holds UTF-8; one never assigned from utf8text is searched as an empty text.
regext
A compiled regular expression. Immutable once compiled: any number of threads may use one at once.
regext%compile
Compiles a pattern with the flags new RegExp(pattern, flags) takes, any of dgimsuvy. On failure stat is
CREINVALIDPATTERN, CREINVALIDFLAGS, CREPATTERNTOOLARGE or CREINVALIDUTF8, and the regular expression is
not compiled. timeout is the time in seconds each match may take before it is abandoned with CREMATCHLIMIT (0
for none); without it the regular expression takes defaultmatchtimeout(), which is none unless set. A timeout
also caps the backtracking memory of a match; without one a match has no limit of time or of memory, so give a
pattern or a text from outside one. edition is the grammar the pattern is read with (a CREEDITION value,
CREEDITIONCURRENT without it), and unicodeversion the version of Unicode whose tables it is read with (a
CREUNICODE value, CREUNICODEDEFAULT without it); under CREEDITIONES2020 the d and v flags are
CREINVALIDFLAGS, and another value of either is CREINVALIDARGUMENT. With stat present a failure is not an
error stop, so compile with stat and a timeout is the form that checks a pattern without a default timeout.

The time in seconds each match may take before it is abandoned with CREMATCHLIMIT (0 for none, and when not
compiled).

The edition whose grammar the pattern was read with, a CREEDITION value (CREEDITIONCURRENT when not compiled).

The interface of , generated from its declarations and their comments by

Constants
EcmaRegexVersion
EcmaRegexVersion is the version of the library.
Types
EEcmaRegex
EEcmaRegex is the class of every exception the engine raises for a pattern, its flags, a text or a match.
EEcmaRegexSyntax
EEcmaRegexSyntax is a pattern that is not valid under the grammar its flags choose. Reason is why, and Offset is the 0-based offset in the pattern's characters (UTF-16 code units without the u or v flag) where it was found.
EEcmaRegexFlags
EEcmaRegexFlags is flags that are not valid: a flag that is not one of dgimsuvy, a flag given twice, or u with v.
EEcmaRegexTooLarge
EEcmaRegexTooLarge is a pattern over one of the limits of size. The pattern was not read to its end, so the error says nothing of whether it is valid.
EEcmaRegexEncoding
EEcmaRegexEncoding is a pattern or a text that is not UTF-8 (or a pattern that is not well-formed UTF-16), which is refused, never read as U+FFFD.
EEcmaRegexTimeout
EEcmaRegexTimeout is a match that ran for longer than its pattern's match timeout. It is not an answer.
EEcmaRegexMemory
EEcmaRegexMemory is a match with a timeout that needed more backtracking memory than its limit. It is not an answer.
TEcmaRegexLimit
TEcmaRegexLimit names a limit of the size of a pattern: its length in bytes of UTF-8, the depth its groups nest, and the size it has when it is read.
TEcmaRegexFlag
The flags of a pattern, as new RegExp(pattern, flags) reads them: d, g, i, m, s, u, v and y.
TEcmaRegexFlags
TEcmaRegexEdition
The edition of ECMA-262 whose grammar a pattern is read with. ereCurrent is today's grammar, ECMAScript 2025, the default. ereEs2020 is the grammar of ECMAScript 2020 (ECMA-262, 11th edition), which JSON Schema 2020-12 names: it refuses what later editions added, and nothing else, the d and v flags, modifier groups such as (?i:...), a group name used by two groups, and a property name or value that is not in the edition's tables. A pattern it accepts has the same answers as in today's grammar, under the same version of Unicode.
TEcmaRegexUnicodeVersion
The version of Unicode whose character database a pattern is read with: the members of each \p{...}, the characters of a group name, and the case folding of the i flag. It is independent of the edition. eruDefault is the version of the V8 the answers are held to, Unicode 17 today, which moves when that V8 moves; eru13 is Unicode 13.0, the version of the year of ECMAScript 2020; eru17 and eru18 are Unicode 17.0 and 18.0; eruLatest is the latest version the library carries, Unicode 18 today, which moves when a later version is added.
TEcmaRegexOptions
A TEcmaRegexOptions is how a pattern is compiled besides its flags: its match timeout in seconds (below 0 for the default, see SetDefaultEcmaRegexMatchTimeout, and 0 for none), the edition whose grammar it is read with and the version of Unicode whose tables it is read with. Default gives the default timeout, today's grammar and V8's Unicode.
TEcmaRegexErrorKind
Why TryCompileEcmaRegex did not compile a pattern: eekSyntax for a pattern that is not valid, eekFlags for flags that are not valid (or that the edition does not have), eekTooLarge for a pattern over a limit of size, eekEncoding for a pattern that is not UTF-8.
TEcmaRegexError
A TEcmaRegexError is the kind and the message of the error TryCompileEcmaRegex gives in place of raising it.
TUtf8Text
A TUtf8Text is UTF-8 text that has been checked once, so that the calls that take it check nothing. A program that matches one text many times makes a TUtf8Text of it and pays for the check once.
TEcmaGroup
A TEcmaGroup is what a group of a match of UTF-8 text holds: whether it took part, its 1-based index and its length in bytes, and its text. A bound between the halves of a character of four bytes (which only a pattern without the u flag can make) is written in Value as U+FFFD.
TEcmaGroups
TEcmaMatch
A TEcmaMatch is a match of UTF-8 text: whether there is one, its 1-based index and length in bytes, its text, and its groups, Groups[0] being the whole match.
TEcmaGroupW
A TEcmaGroupW is what a group of a match of UTF-16 text holds, in code units.
TEcmaGroupsW
TEcmaMatchW
A TEcmaMatchW is a match of UTF-16 text, in code units.
TEcmaMatchArray
TEcmaMatchArrayW
TEcmaCaptures
A TEcmaCaptures holds the bounds of the groups of a match, kept from one match to the next so that matching allocates nothing once it has room for the pattern's groups. Range reports the 1-based index and the length of group G (0 for the whole match), in the units of the text that was matched, and false for a group that did not take part.

An IEcmaRegex is a compiled pattern. It is safe to share between threads.

Title: "PHP: API reference"
The PHP API of the extension, namespace , generated from the classes and functions
 gives PHP and their doc comments by . Getting started
shows it at work.
Regex
A compiled ECMA-262 regular expression, as  compiles it.
Regex::DEFAULTUNICODEVERSION
The version of Unicode a pattern is read with by default: the version of the V8 the answers are held to.
Regex::LATESTUNICODEVERSION
The newest version of Unicode the extension carries, which 'latest' stands for.
Regex::construct
Compiles a pattern with the flags  takes, any of dgimsuvy. Throws
InvalidPatternException, InvalidFlagsException or PatternTooLargeException (each a RegexException). $timeout is
the time in seconds each match may take before it is abandoned with MatchLimitException (0 for none); null takes
Regex::defaultTimeout(), which is none unless set. A timeout also caps the backtracking memory of a match;
without one a match has no limit of time or of memory, so give a pattern or a text from outside one.
$edition is the grammar the pattern is read with: 'current' (today's, the default) or 'es2020', the grammar of
ECMAScript 2020, which JSON Schema 2020-12 names. It refuses what later editions added, and nothing else: the d
and v flags (InvalidFlagsException), modifier groups such as (?i:...), a group name used by two groups, and a
property name or value that is not in that edition's tables (InvalidPatternException). $unicodeversion is the
version of Unicode whose tables the pattern is read with: null (the default, DEFAULTUNICODEVERSION), 13, 17, 18
or 'latest' (LATESTUNICODEVERSION). Each is independent of the other; both are settled here, and cost a match
nothing. A value of either outside those throws a ValueError.
Regex::setDefaultTimeout
Sets the timeout of every Regex made from now on without one of its own: seconds, or null (or 0) for no limit,
the default. It is the process-wide default of .NET's REGEXDEFAULTMATCHTIMEOUT; a program that matches
patterns or subjects from outside should set one when it starts. A Regex already made keeps its own.
Regex::defaultTimeout
The timeout in seconds of a Regex made now without one of its own, or null for no limit.
Regex::timeout
The time in seconds each match may take before it is abandoned with MatchLimitException, or null for none.
Regex::isValid
Whether a pattern is valid with the flags, in the edition and the version of Unicode (as the constructor takes
them), without compiling it.
Regex::edition
The edition whose grammar the pattern was read with: 'current' or 'es2020'.
Regex::unicodeVersion
The version of Unicode whose tables the pattern was read with, resolved: 13, 17 or 18.
Regex::unicodeVersions
The versions of Unicode the extension carries, each a set of tables a pattern can be read with.
Regex::source
The pattern as it was given.
Regex::flags
The flags as RegExp.prototype.flags writes them, in the order dgimsuvy.
Regex::groupCount
The number of capturing groups.
Regex::groupNames
The distinct names of the groups, in the order of the first group of each name.
Regex::test
Whether the pattern matches at or after $offset (at $offset alone with the y flag), as RegExp.prototype.test
with lastIndex set to it. A match that reaches the pattern's timeout throws MatchLimitException; a timeout in
seconds here takes its place for this match (0 for none).
Regex::exec
The first match at or after $offset, as exec finds it with lastIndex set to it: a MatchResult, or null. A match
that reaches the pattern's timeout throws MatchLimitException; a timeout in seconds here takes its place.
Regex::matchAll
Every match of a global search, as matchAll makes one: an array of MatchResult. After an empty match the
search goes on one character later, and with the y flag each match must start where the one before ended. A
match that reaches the pattern's timeout throws MatchLimitException.
Regex::countMatches
The number of matches of a global search, without making them.
Regex::replace
The subject with the first match replaced, or every match with the g flag, as String.prototype.replace replaces
them. The replacement is a template ($& the match, ` `` the text before it, $' the text after it, $1 to $99 a
group, $\<name> a named group, $$ a dollar sign) or a callable given each MatchResult, returning the text.
Regex::replaceAll

Title: "Compatibility"
What a change must do so that code built against an earlier release keeps working, and which check enforces each
rule. The reasons are in the plan.
Two things reach a consumer from an earlier release and meet a later one:
Generated code. A holder written by the source generator, or by a code generator that takes
  , is compiled into the consumer's assembly with the version of the
  emitter it was written by. The application may load any later version of the library. The holder calls public
  members hidden from editors, and passes the library a compiled image of its regular expression.
Compiled code. An assembly built against one version runs against a later one.
Within a major version, both must keep working, and an image must keep being read wherever it is still right.
Images
An image () records four things, and a reader decides from them whether to read it or to compile
the pattern instead. Either way the answers are the same; an image only saves the work of building.
  What   Where   The reader  
    
  The layout    in the header, and the body's sections   Reads every layout from  to . Skips a section it does not know that is optional, ignores the image for one that is required.  
  The instructions   The opcodes of , by number   Ignores an image with a number it does not know.  
  The compiler    in the header   Ignores an image from below .  
  The settings   The flags, the edition and the resolved Unicode version   Ignores an image written for others.  
An ignored image raises the  event of the  event source, with the reason, and on
.NET counts it in the  counter.
What a change does
  Change   What to do   What checks it  
    
  A refactoring, a comment, the validator, anything that changes nothing the compiler writes   Nothing.   The golden check passes unchanged.  
  The compiler writes something different for some pattern, with the same answers (smaller, faster)   Raise .   The golden check fails on changed output under an unchanged revision.  
  The compiler writes something different because what it wrote gave wrong answers   Raise , and set  to the new revision. Say so in the release notes: generated code built before it compiles its patterns when first used, until it is generated again.   The golden check, which then expects the older images to be ignored.  
  A new instruction   Add it to  with the next number. Never reuse or renumber one.   .  
  An instruction that is to do something different   A new instruction. The old number keeps its old meaning.   , and the golden check.  
  A new fact the matcher stores in a program or an automaton   Derive it from the facts older images hold, or treat its absence as the conservative value. If neither is possible, write it in a new required section, so older images are ignored rather than misread.   The golden check.  
  Something new that a reader may skip   A new optional section, with a tag no section has had.   The golden check.  
  A change to the header or to how sections are framed   A new . Keep reading the older layouts.   The golden check.  
  A new public member   Add it to  (or  for one only the .NET build has).   The public API analyzers fail the build otherwise.  
  A change to or removal of a public member, the members generated code calls included   Only in a major version.   The public API analyzers, and package validation against the last release.  
  Dropping a layout, an instruction or a section from what is read   Only in a major version.   The golden check.

body:

PublicationStatus: Published

Title: "Benchmarks: the Industry workloads"
Corvus.Regex.Ecma262 is faster than  almost everywhere, and it gives V8's answers
where .NET doesn't. On the Industry workloads that .NET itself publishes figures for, a typical night looks like
this.
The interpreter is at or below .NET's interpreter on all but three of the workloads they both answer, and takes
  about a third of the time at the median.
The generated code is at or below .NET's generated code on about nine workloads in ten, over UTF-16 and over UTF-8
  alike. It takes about three quarters of the time at the median over UTF-16, and about three fifths over UTF-8.
Both are far ahead of V8, which takes about seven times as long at the median.
The exact figures are on the benchmark page, where every
engine is measured on one runner each night.
The library is measured against  and against V8 on the Industry workload set of
dotnet/performance (): the Sherlock Holmes text and
the Rust  patterns, the Leipzig corpus searches, the mariomka email, URI and IPv4 patterns, and the rebar
name searches over Russian and Chinese subtitles. These are the sets behind .NET's own "regex performance
improvements in .NET N" posts, so the figures can be read beside theirs.
The figures
The figures are on one page, corvus-oss.org/corvus-regex-ecma262-benchmarks. Each night it runs every Corvus
ECMA-262 engine's published harness image, this library's among them, one after another on one runner, so every
figure on it was measured on the same machine in the same night. Pick the engines and the measure, and read the
leaderboard, the matrix of every workload, one workload at a time with its spread, or two engines head to head.
Each engine's ECMA-262 compliance is beside its name, its header says which release of each engine ran, and every
day's data is kept.
No table of figures is repeated here. A table in a document goes stale the night after it's written, and the page doesn't.
What is measured
Six engines, each counting the matches of every workload over its whole text (, one call per operation):
  Engine   What it is  
   
  .NET interpreter    with   
  .NET generated    through   
  Corvus interpreter   this library's interpreter over UTF-16  
  Corvus generated UTF-16   this library's source generator over UTF-16  
  Corvus generated UTF-8   this library's source generator over the same text as UTF-8 bytes, nothing transcoded  
  V8 (Node 24)   Node's , the oracle of the test data, over the same texts, counted by a  loop that advances  as  does ()  
The Corvus and V8 rows run under the  flag, which .NET has no mode for, so the two read a few patterns by
different rules. On three workloads .NET counts something other than V8 does:  and the  of
 with , where ECMA-262 counts CR as a line terminator and .NET doesn't, and
, where .NET's  takes letters and digits of every script. A count other than V8's is a wrong answer, so the
benchmark page shows .NET's figures on those three as failures (✕), with both counts in the tooltip. This library
counts as V8 does on every workload.
The figures on the benchmark page are measured under the interleaved protocol of every Corvus engine's harness
(, ): every workload in turn, each in three rounds
of the engines in turn, their order turned each round, each figure a process of its own, warmed for at least 1.5 s
(.NET compiles a method again as it is used, and needs that long to reach its final code) and timed for 0.7 s in seven
passes. The bar is the median of the rounds and the whisker the fastest and the slowest round; a row's ratio is read
against its neighbours' rather than to the last few percent. The BenchmarkDotNet classes of the same project
(, ) measure the same counts under the pinned-host procedure, with what each
allocates; the library allocates nothing per match once its working memory has grown.
Where this library is slower than .NET, and why
Three kinds of row read above 1.0 against .NET's generated code. Each is the price of an ECMA-262 rule that .NET
doesn't apply.
Case-insensitive patterns under the u flag. The search must find the long s and the Kelvin sign as forms of
    and , which .NET's search ignores, so its tables carry every form ( with ).
A class that admits a supplementary character before a literal at a fixed distance. Such a character is two
   units, so the distance is not fixed and the literal is found by a walk back rather than at an offset
   ().
Non-ASCII literals over UTF-8. Every Cyrillic or Chinese character is two or three bytes with no rare byte
   among them, where UTF-16 gives the search one rare unit per character; so the UTF-8 rows for the Chinese names
   read above .NET over UTF-16 while the UTF-16 rows are level.
The other rows above 1.0 are within a few percent of parity and read either side of it from run to run: both engines
are at the floor of one vectorised search over the tex
